title: Fix registered replay descendant cleanup on command exit
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Registered replay currently cleans up child solvers only after a timeout. If a command leader exits normally or with an error, its descendants can keep running and modify outputs after `run_command` has returned. A ready-child fixture on the pinned baseline reproduced a post-return write for both exit 0 and exit 7.

Move cleanup into `finally`: on POSIX, signal the owned process group after success, failure, timeout or interruption, tolerate an already-finished group, and reap the leader. Preserve the leader's exit status, timeout failure, assertion-enabled child environment, explicit optimization options and all verification commands/source checks. Extend PR1484's real parent/child/grandchild fixture to cover the new boundaries and document the lifecycle contract.

This is **verification engineering**, not a mathematical result or performance improvement. The selected conditional κ remains `0.001672660197076918`. Verification commands still must join their proof-relevant children and propagate their errors; terminating an unfinished solver does not certify its result. Detached sessions/groups are outside scope. Windows keeps tree cleanup while the leader is alive; this does not solve native Windows cleanup after leader exit.

## Task and overlap

Canonical base and final refreshed main: **`0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`**, priority revision **4**. Explicit card `portable-replay`, scope key `831cc1a3c8f9ff01b197`; **scope changed** from cross-environment/payload comparison to a reproducible replay lifetime defect. This protects bounded verification and output stability without changing mathematical coverage. Selection was restricted and deliberate, not a uniform random assignment.

The three candidates were: selected native BIT reserve coefficient (already covered by #2084/#2120), emitted owner-map binding (already audited in #2301 and repaired by #2355), and this process-lifetime boundary. The last had a concrete small failing experiment and no equivalent repair in the reviewed live evidence. The helper's nonce was not used as a novelty or test-randomness claim.

Nearest predecessor: Paul Romeo's **#1484**, head `225cc15f88732ef86f48b75e34a9422bcb664993`, tests timeout cleanup with a live leader. This adds the distinct already-exited leader and interrupted-wait cases. **#1298**, head `e76026571dbfa7299bf474b941c9abeb5bd556b3`, supplied related portability work. No pending predecessor code is imported. Both are merged.

The exact original implementation and tests are identified by the base above: `scripts/research_package.py` and `tests/test_research_process_tree.py`. Only these two files and the package guide change. A bounded fresh overlap search covered 572 open PRs (including drafts), 1084 Discussion/comment/reply records and 1536 local notes/ledger records with complete pagination and no warnings; arbitrary diffs are outside that search. A single coordination-claim attempt in discussion #1472 was rejected by the integration, so no public claim was posted.

## Validation

Linux x86_64, CPython 3.12.14, repository code executed without inherited credentials:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_baseline.py
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py' -v
python3 -O -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py' -v
python3 -B tests/test_research_process_tree.py -v
python3 -O -B tests/test_research_process_tree.py -v
git diff --check HEAD^
```

- Baseline: `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.
- All **69 affected tests pass in each mode**, with no skips. The seven process-tree tests also pass in each mode from a Git-free export of the committed files in a path containing spaces.
- The new success/error/interruption tests run against the **original pinned function** produce three expected failures, each detecting live descendants. Fixture teardown stops them.
- Deliberately replacing group cleanup with leader-only cleanup is detected for timeout and for both leader exit codes. Ordinary fully joined completion remains a positive control.
- The same two post-return-write fixtures change from **2/2 writes before** to **0/2 after**; exit 7 still reports the original command failure.
- Working tree and final diff are clean; no mathematical source or selected certificate changes.

No unexpected test failure remains. Full supplier/cold/historical package replays, native Windows/macOS execution, proof-assistant builds and hosted CI were not run locally. Since this changes shared replay controls, the existing CI planner may select all registered packages; no invalidation rule is weakened.

## Credit

Credit Douglas Colkitt and retained contributors for the replay launcher, and Paul Romeo for PR1484's process-tree tests and earlier portability work. Prepared for **yssite with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance** in investigation, implementation, verification and writing. No independent human review is claimed. Apache-2.0; existing attribution remains intact.

## Open next questions

Native Windows cleanup after leader exit needs a separate bounded investigation, likely a native lifetime primitive rather than a late `taskkill` call. First reproduce the same ready-child/early-exit cases on Windows; the blocker here is the absence of a native Windows validation environment. Deliberately detached descendants would require stronger containment, not a larger process-group claim. Neither extension is included in this fix.
